# PFW-002: Inbound traffic is denied by default at the provider

- **Group:** Provider firewall
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** not needed

## Why it matters

A firewall that only lists what to block leaves every new service open. On a stateless firewall, a permit that matches only a source port (TCP from source port 443, say) also opens every port to a sender that picks that port, so it fails this check for TCP; UDP source port rules are judged in PFW-003. A Hetzner Cloud Firewall drops inbound traffic no rule permits as soon as it is attached. The OVH Edge Network Firewall is the opposite: a packet no rule matches is allowed, and only a final rule that denies every IPv4 packet makes it default deny.

## Verify by hand

```sh
OVH: the rule list of the address ends with a deny rule for protocol IPv4 from any source (OVH's own example uses sequence 19)
```

## How to fix it

OVH: add a last rule (sequence 19) that denies protocol IPv4 from any source, after the permit rules for your services and for return traffic

## What a fix can break

Without the return traffic rules of PFW-007 in front of it, a final deny drops the replies to every connection the host opens.
